header: An identifier is not an amount. A bank account number, a policy number, a cheque number, an IFSC code, a ticket or circular number is a label: I copy its digits as the circular prints them, in one unbroken run, never grouped with commas ("34,42,04,00,623") and never turned into a number (a 16 to 18 digit number loses its last digits in a JavaScript number). Rupee amounts keep their Indian digit grouping. This module is the one place that tells the two apart, for the engine (text it writes) and the screen (cells it draws). Pure, no imports.

symbols.name: ID_WORDS
doc: Words that say a number is a label, not a sum.

symbols.name: isIdentifierLabel
symbols.sig: export function isIdentifierLabel(label: string | undefined | null): boolean
doc: A heading of a column (or a label before a number) that names an identifier.

symbols.name: isLongDigitRun
doc: A run of digits that can only be an identifier: nine or more digits with no decimal part, no rupee sign, no "/-". I treat amounts of a crore or more as written with the rupee sign or a word.

symbols.name: stripIdentifierSeparators
symbols.sig: export function stripIdentifierSeparators(text: string): { text: string; changed: string[] }
doc: Returns the text with the separators taken out of the digit runs that are identifiers: after a word like "account number", "A/c", "policy", "cheque", "IFSC", "ticket" (within a few characters), and any run of nine or more digits that was grouped by commas or spaces without a rupee sign before it. Anything with a rupee sign, "Rs", a decimal point or "/-" is an amount, and I do not touch it.

behaviours: an account number after its label loses the commas
also in the western grouping and with spaces
a policy and a cheque number
an unbroken number is left as it is
a rupee amount keeps its grouping
a grouped amount with no label and fewer than nine digits is an amount
a grouped run of nine digits or more with no rupee sign is an identifier
a date or a year is untouched
labels: account, IFSC, policy, cheque are identifier labels; amount, premium, rent are not
nine digits or more is a long run; a year and an amount are not
